name: BC Broussard
profile: Listed as a co-founder of HomeLight (San Francisco real-estate agent-matching platform founded 2012; valued ~$1.6B in 2021) alongside Drew Uher and Jason Zhang in MarketScreener/Zippia listings. HomeLight's own materials and Wikipedia credit only Drew Uher as founder/CEO; no biography of Broussard was found.
notes: Thin public footprint: only aggregator listings (marketscreener.com Drew Uher relations page, zippia.com/homelight-careers-1415353) name BC Broussard as HomeLight co-founder; current role unknown. Wikipedia credits Drew Uher alone. Verify via HomeLight before outreach.

name: Mark Gainey
profile: Reno-raised Harvard grad (AB Fine Arts, 1990) who co-founded enterprise email software firm Kana Communications with Michael Horvath in 1996 and took it public in 1999. In 2009 the pair co-founded Strava; Gainey was its first CEO and CEO again 2013-2017, and remains executive chairman of the ~$2.2B fitness social network.
interesting_fact: Gainey and Horvath met on Harvard's rowing crew in the 1980s; Strava's name comes from the Swedish word 'sträva', meaning 'strive'.
deep_cut_fact: He only took up rowing at Harvard after a running injury in his freshman year, joining the varsity lightweight crew; before startups he spent 1991-1995 at private equity firm TA Associates.
notes: Press email on PR Newswire is Cloudflare-obfuscated (decodes to press@strava.com). Has done podcasts (Rich Roll, Antler Early Days, Terra) - receptive to long-form interviews.

name: Alex Buttle
current_role: Co-founder, Motorway (UK online used-car selling platform)
profile: UK serial entrepreneur who co-founded Motorway in July 2017 with Tom Leathes and Harry Jones, a team that had already built several startups together including the UK's biggest broadband price-comparison site (acquired by uSwitch). Motorway connects car sellers with 8,000+ verified dealers and passed a $1B valuation in 2021.
interesting_fact: Motorway's founding trio has worked together since meeting in 2002; Motorway is their fifth startup together, after ventures including a broadband comparison site, a travel accommodation curation site and an office-space search site.
deep_cut_fact: Writing as a Motorway director in a City AM debate column, Buttle argued that 2035 was too soon for the UK to ban new petrol and diesel car sales.
notes: Low public profile; CEO Tom Leathes is the company's usual spokesperson. Exact current title not listed on motorway.co.uk/about (an earlier version listed him as Co-founder & VP Growth per search snippet).

name: Philipp Triebel
current_role: Co-founder and former co-CEO of SellerX (Berlin Amazon-brand aggregator); stepped down June 2024. Current venture not publicly confirmed.
profile: German entrepreneur and Harvard Business School 2010 graduate who co-founded SellerX in Berlin in 2020 with Malte Horeyseck; the Amazon-seller aggregator raised heavily (incl. a $500M round in Nov 2021) and hit unicorn status. Both co-CEOs left in June 2024. Earlier he co-founded IVY, a New York 'social university' events community, and worked in investing (Accrete Capital, Praxi Partners per listings).
interesting_fact: Before SellerX he co-founded IVY, a 'social university' that by 2017 had 150,000+ subscribers and ran 1,000+ events a year across seven US cities; he and co-founder Beri Meric first toyed with a members-only dating network.
deep_cut_fact: On IVY's group trips he said: 'I made good friends in business school by traveling with them' - and that members 'all come back best friends.'
notes: Left SellerX June 2024 (per Sifted/OMR: https://omr.com/de/daily/thrasio-klone-scheitern-sellerx-bbg-razor-group). A self-maintained profile lists a stealth startup from April 2025 (unverified). Aggregator business model has struggled - avoid that topic. No published contact found; LinkedIn likely best route.

name: Kam Ghaffarian
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, Axiom Space; founder of X-energy; co-founder of Intuitive Machines and Quantum Space
profile: Iranian-born American engineer-entrepreneur who moved to the US at 17. Co-founded NASA contractor Stinger Ghaffarian Technologies (sold to KBR for $355M in 2018), then built a space-and-energy portfolio: X-energy (high-temperature gas-cooled nuclear reactors, 2009), Intuitive Machines (Moon lander, public via SPAC 2023), Axiom Space (private space station, 2016) and Quantum Space (2020).
interesting_fact: Watching the 1969 Apollo 11 landing on TV in Iran sparked his interest in space; decades later his Intuitive Machines lander touched down on the Moon on Feb 22, 2024. His X-energy nuclear reactor company makes him directly relevant to energy/data-center power.
deep_cut_fact: As keynote speaker at Capitol Technology University's May 2, 2026 commencement (his alma mater: BS 1983, PhD 2022), he surprised every graduate crossing the stage with $1,500 in a gold envelope.
notes: Also founded nonprofit Limitless Space Institute (2019). X-energy (nuclear SMRs) is the strongest angle for an energy/data-center podcast; X-energy's press office is an alternative route.

name: Adam R. Gerchen
current_role: CEO, Gerchen Capital Partners (Chicago); co-founder of Heyday and Keller Postman
profile: Chicago-based investor and litigation-finance pioneer (Brown, Harvard Law; ex-Goldman Sachs and Alyeska). Co-founded Gerchen Keller Capital in 2013, which raised $2B+ before its 2016 sale to Burford Capital, where he became President; co-founded law firm Keller Postman. In 2020 he co-founded Heyday, an Amazon-brand aggregator that raised $175M Series A and a $555M Series C.
interesting_fact: Gerchen Keller Capital became the largest private investment firm focused exclusively on legal and regulatory risk within about three years of launch, raising over $2B in institutional capital before Burford acquired it.
deep_cut_fact: At Harvard Law School he was President of the Harvard Association of Law and Business; he graduated Brown Phi Beta Kappa, magna cum laude.
notes: Heyday co-founded Aug 2020 with CEO Sebastian Rymarz (https://prnewswire.com/news-releases/heyday-emerges-from-stealth-with-175m-series-a-funding-to-accelerate-marketplace-native-brands-301175394.html); aggregators list Gerchen as executive chairman 2020-2024. Not to be confused with Heyday skincare. Firm website is JS-only; no published email found.

name: Davis Siksnans
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Printful; Senior Advisor at Draugiem Group (since June 2022) and angel investor
profile: Latvian entrepreneur who co-founded print-on-demand company Printful with Lauris Liberts in 2013 out of Latvia's Draugiem Group, and was CEO from 2015 to June 2022. Printful became Latvia's first unicorn in 2021 after a $130M investment from Bregal Sagemount, and in late 2024 agreed to merge with rival Printify (combined group named Fyul).
interesting_fact: Printful was spun out of Startup Vitamins, the team's online store selling motivational-quote posters for startups; frustration with third-party printers led them to build their own printing operation.
deep_cut_fact: Printful launched on July 16, 2013 with a three-person team printing t-shirts in co-founder Lauris Liberts's garage; Siksnans's motto: 'A good time to start is anytime, because a better one will never come.'
notes: Stepped down as CEO June 29, 2022 (https://www.printful.com/news/printful-management-team-change). Frequent podcast guest (Mixergy, Hack the Entrepreneur, Wix 'Now What'). No published direct email found; LinkedIn is likely best route.

name: Liu Yanfang
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director and Chief Technology Officer, XTransfer (Shanghai)
profile: Chinese technologist (刘艳芳) who co-founded XTransfer in 2017 with CEO Bill (Guobiao) Deng and other ex-Alibaba/Ant Group colleagues; she leads engineering as CTO. XTransfer is a B2B cross-border payments platform for Chinese SME exporters, valued at $3.02B after its March 2026 Series E, and filed for a Hong Kong main-board IPO in April 2026.
interesting_fact: XTransfer says it is the world's largest B2B cross-border trade payment platform by volume, with 2025 payment volume of ~$60.5B, ~897,000 registered clients and over 98.5% of transactions reviewed automatically by AI.
deep_cut_fact: Before XTransfer she was a senior technical expert in Alibaba's B2B business unit, where she built Alibaba B2B's financial product management framework and its payment solutions from scratch.
notes: Very low English-language profile; CEO Bill Deng is the public face. Company site lists only customer helpdesk/complaints emails, no press email. Chinese-language outreach via the company is the likely route; HK IPO prospectus (2026) has her official bio.

name: Florian Fournier
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Orasio (European AI video-analysis/defence-tech startup); co-founder and board member, PayFit
profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded Paris payroll/HR SaaS PayFit in 2015 with Firmin Zocchetto and Ghislain de Fontenay and spent nine years building it into a ~$2B company. He left his operational role in January 2024 and in 2025 launched Orasio, which raised a EUR16M seed led by Frst to build sovereign European AI that analyses video feeds for police, cities, critical sites and the military.
interesting_fact: Orasio's name comes from the Greek 'orasi' ('vision'); its AI detects fires, falls, crowd movements and weapons in real time, and France's defence ministry AI agency (Amiad) has taken up its image-analysis tools.
deep_cut_fact: A Polytechnique alumnus who also attended a military school, he met both Orasio co-founders (Arnaud Delaunay and Fabio Gennari) back in preparatory school; he says 'J'ai toujours eu une sensibilité forte pour les enjeux de défense.'
notes: Media-friendly: Orasio's press page lists his interviews with BFM Business, Europe 1, BFMTV etc. French-language outreach likely best. LinkedIn link is the company page, not personal.

name: Diogo Frenkel
current_role: Co-founder and CFO, Dock (Brazilian payments/banking-infrastructure company, formerly Conductor) - title as of 2021; current status not confirmed
profile: Brazilian fintech executive listed as co-founder and CFO of Dock, the Sao Paulo-area payments and banking-as-a-service provider that grew out of card processor Conductor (founded 1999). In 2021 Conductor, Dock and Muxi were unified under the Dock brand; Dock reached unicorn status in 2022 (~$1.5B) and serves 400+ companies in 11 Latin American countries.
interesting_fact: Dock started as an in-house project inside card processor Conductor in 2018; it became the name for the whole company in 2021 because it was the only pillar built entirely in-house, and in 2023 Dock became a Central Bank of Brazil-regulated institution.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal bio or post-2021 coverage found. CEO Antonio Soares is Dock's spokesperson. Sources conflict on founding history (Conductor 1999 vs Dock 2014/2018). Portuguese-language outreach via Dock press room recommended.

name: Avi Meir
profile: Serial founder who co-founded Hotel Ninjas (sold to Booking.com in 2014) and then founded TravelPerk in Barcelona in 2015 to bring consumer-grade tech to business travel. Rebranded Perk in Nov 2025 as an AI-native travel and spend platform, it passed $300M annualized revenue with 10,000+ customer companies and moved to dual HQs in London and Boston.
interesting_fact: When COVID made business travel effectively illegal in early 2020, Meir cut costs without layoffs, kept hiring engineers and bought two competitors cheaply; ARR went from ~$20M pre-pandemic to over $300M.
deep_cut_fact: He likens his pandemic playbook to a hibernating bear ('preserve the core, lose the fat'), and says the lesson he took from Booking.com after selling Hotel Ninjas was that 'winning globally means building locally.'
notes: Rebrand announced Nov 4, 2025 (https://www.perk.com/press-release/travelperk-rebrands-to-perk-the-intelligent-platform-powering-real-work/). Talkative, candid interviewee; IPO talk in recent coverage.

name: Anthony Watson
current_role: Founder of The Bank of London (CEO until September 2024); current executive role not confirmed
profile: London-born technology executive (CBE, 2023) who was CIO of Barclays' retail bank (launching the Pingit app) and Nike's CIO in 2014, then co-founded crypto platform Uphold in 2015. He conceived The Bank of London in 2016 and launched it in November 2021 as a UK clearing, correspondent and wholesale bank, serving as CEO until September 2024.
interesting_fact: The Bank of London launched on 30 November 2021 as the UK's sixth clearing bank; Watson is also a prominent LGBT advocate - GLAAD board member since 2013, Stonewall ambassador and founder of The Watson Pride Foundation.
deep_cut_fact: He studied theology and considered becoming a minister, but a part-time job at AOL Ireland during his degree hooked him on technology; he then joined First-e, billed as Europe's first internet bank.
notes: Left Bank of London CEO role Sept 2024; the bank has had difficult press since - avoid that topic. anthonywatson.com is a parked domain (not his). No published contact found; LinkedIn or GLAAD/Stonewall networks are possible routes. Also an art collector (18th-19th c. portraits, contemporary works).

name: Matias de Tezanos
current_role: Founder and CEO, PeopleFund (multi-family office / global tech investor); co-founder, HealthCare.com
profile: Costa Rican-born serial internet entrepreneur who founded Hoteles.com at about 20 (later acquired by Expedia), co-founded ad network ClickDiario (sold to Fox International Channels in 2006), led US insurance marketplace BrokersWeb (2008-2011) and co-founded health-insurance platform HealthCare.com (Inc. 500's #1 insurance company in 2019). He now invests globally via PeopleFund, founded 2012.
interesting_fact: Named a World Economic Forum Young Global Leader in 2009; his PeopleFund portfolio reportedly includes stakes in 12 unicorns among 30+ companies, and he was building an agri-tech venture turning plastic into biodegradable products (2023).
deep_cut_fact: He first went online in 1994 while on holiday in Punta del Este, Uruguay (Costa Rica had no access for him yet) - and publicly thanked Uruguay for it at the Punta Tech Meetup; website-building began as a hobby before Hoteles.com.
notes: Lives in Costa Rica (per El Observador 2023). matiasdetezanos.com is a parked domain, not his. PeopleFund site contact form is the only published route found. Spanish-language outreach may help.

name: Jacques Fu
current_role: Founder, PETE (PETE Learning, per Crunchbase); former co-founder and CTO of Stax Payments (formerly Fattmerchant)
profile: Orlando technologist and University of Central Florida alum who was co-founder and founding CTO of Stax (originally Fattmerchant), the subscription-pricing payments processor started in 2014 with Suneera Madhani and Sal Rehmetullah. Stax passed $100M in recurring revenue and was valued at $1B+ after a $245M Series D in 2021, becoming Orlando's first unicorn. He has since founded PETE and invests in startups.
interesting_fact: Stax was Orlando's first startup to reach unicorn status; its model - flat monthly subscription instead of per-transaction payment fees - grew out of Madhani selling payment terminals from her VW Beetle.
notes: Co-founded the Orlando Devs developer meetup community (per search snippets of SpeakerHub/Crunchbase; pages returned 503, so unverified). A podcast lists him as author of a book 'Time Hacks' (unverified). Profile pages: https://drupal.speakerhub.com/speaker/jacques-fu, https://crunchbase.com/person/jacques-fu. No published email found.

name: Peter Phillips
current_role: Listed as Co-founder & Chief Business Officer, Colossal Biosciences (as of 2022); current status not confirmed
profile: Listed as a co-founder and Chief Business Officer of Colossal Biosciences, the Dallas-based de-extinction company launched in 2021 by CEO Ben Lamm and geneticist George Church, which is working to bring back the woolly mammoth, thylacine (Tasmanian tiger) and dodo. No independent biography of Phillips was found.
interesting_fact: Colossal's thylacine project is run in partnership with the University of Melbourne; Phillips appears in Colossal's March 2022 leadership team line-up as chief business officer.
notes: Very thin footprint: founder listing at https://invest.microventures.com/stock/colossal-laboratories-bioscience and a 2022 Dallas Innovates caption are the only sources. Common name - verify identity before outreach. colossal.com pages blocked (403); search results suggest press releases list emily@colossal.com as media contact but this was not verified in-session.

name: Henry Kim
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Swiftly (Seattle retail-technology platform for grocers)
profile: Serial e-commerce entrepreneur who was previously co-founder and president of Symphony Commerce. In 2018 he co-founded Swiftly with ex-Symphony colleagues Sean Turner and Karen Ho to give brick-and-mortar supermarkets e-commerce, loyalty and retail-media tools; the company moved from the Bay Area to Seattle in 2019 and became a unicorn after a $100M round led by BRV.
interesting_fact: Swiftly's pitch is helping independent and regional grocers fight Amazon-style competition; Kim warns 'Retailers need to act now to connect the digital and in-store experience' or lose loyal customers and ad revenue.
notes: Common name - Swiftly is the anchor. A Frontlines.io podcast bio (https://frontlines.io/podcasts/henry-kim) reportedly says he once owned Orange Julius and Dairy Queen franchises and founded a comic-book-and-sushi restaurant concept sold in 1997 - could not load page (429) to verify, so not used as deep-cut. No published press email found.

name: Will Warren
current_role: Co-founder and board member, 0x Labs (0x protocol / Matcha); transitioned out of co-CEO role in 2026
profile: Co-founder of 0x, the Ethereum decentralized-exchange infrastructure protocol whose API and Matcha aggregator route billions in on-chain trades. He co-wrote the original 0x white paper with Amir Bandeali in February 2017 and led 0x Labs as CEO/co-CEO; in 2026 he stepped back from the co-CEO role, with Bandeali taking sole leadership.
interesting_fact: Warren and Amir Bandeali started building 0x in 2016 and published the white paper 'An open protocol for decentralized exchange on the Ethereum blockchain' in February 2017, ahead of the 2017 ZRX token launch.
deep_cut_fact: He came to crypto from hard science rather than software: before co-founding 0x he did applied physics work at Los Alamos National Laboratory (per Messari's 0x profile, which lists him as co-founder & CEO).
notes: Co-CEO step-down reported by The Defiant (https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/will-warren-steps-down-0x-co-ceo-7kxgji), dated May 2026 per search results. Active in crypto circles (ETHDenver speaker). Personal X handle not verified in-session.

name: Philip Leung
current_role: Scientist on the molecule-design team at Xaira Therapeutics (Seattle); self-described co-founder per profile aggregators
profile: Protein-design scientist (Philip J. Y. Leung) trained in David Baker's lab at the University of Washington Institute for Protein Design (NSF Graduate Fellow, then postdoc) who joined AI drug-discovery company Xaira Therapeutics, launched in 2024 with $1B+ from ARCH, Foresite and others. IPD names Baker, Watson and Bennett as Xaira co-founders; Leung's founder status is only claimed on aggregator profiles.
interesting_fact: He is a co-author of the 2025 Nature RFantibody study - AI that designs antibodies from scratch - whose technology Xaira licensed; IPD notes Leung is employed by Xaira.
deep_cut_fact: He co-led (with Susana Vazquez-Torres and Preetham Venkatesh) the 2023 Baker Lab project in which AI-designed proteins bound helical peptide hormones such as glucagon with the highest affinity ever reported for a computer-generated protein without experimental optimization.
notes: Founder claim uncertain: Xaira launch releases and IPD don't list him as a co-founder; aggregator village.ai does. GeekWire 2024 calls him a former IPD postdoc on Xaira's design team. Baker lab alumni page may list a different venture (search snippet: 'Co-Founder, Sealth Biotech') - unverified. Early-career scientist; outreach via Xaira or academic channels.
